title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array

analysis.problem_summary: Find all numbers from 1 to n that do not appear in the input array of size n.
analysis.intuition: By storing all seen numbers in a Hash Set, we can check whether any number from 1 to n is present in O(1) average time.
approach: Iterate through the array `nums` and insert every element into a `HashSet`.
Iterate through all candidate numbers from `1` to `n` (inclusive).
Check if the `HashSet` contains the current number.
If the number is missing from the set, append it to the result list.
analysis.why_it_works: A hash set allows constant time average lookups, enabling us to easily identify which integers in the sequence 1 through n were omitted.
analysis.key_takeaway: Using a HashSet provides a direct and easy-to-understand solution for tracking element presence, though it requires O(n) extra space.
analysis.time_explanation: Populating the hash set takes O(n) time, and checking numbers 1 through n takes O(n) time, giving an overall linear runtime.
analysis.space_explanation: The HashSet stores up to n distinct elements from the array, taking O(n) auxiliary space.

analysis.problem_summary: Find all missing numbers in the range [1, n] without using extra space.
analysis.intuition: Since all numbers are within range [1, n], each number `x` corresponds to a valid array index `x - 1`. We can mark the presence of `x` by making the element at index `x - 1` negative.
approach: Determine the corresponding target index as `idx = Math.abs(num) - 1`.
If the element at `nums[idx]` is positive, negate it to signify that `idx + 1` exists in the array.
Perform a second pass over `nums`: for any index `i` where `nums[i]` remains positive, `i + 1` was never encountered, so append `i + 1` to the output list.
analysis.why_it_works: The absolute value allows us to read original values even after they have been negated, effectively utilizing the array's sign bit as a boolean visited flag without losing information.
analysis.key_takeaway: When input values map directly to valid array indices ([1, n] to [0, n-1]), the sign of elements can be repurposed as in-place visited flags to achieve O(1) auxiliary space.
analysis.time_explanation: The algorithm makes two linear scans over the array of size n, resulting in O(n) runtime.
analysis.space_explanation: All operations modify the array in-place. The output list does not count as extra space as per the problem description, so auxiliary space complexity is O(1).
